# Writing for Agents Skill for Muse

A craft reference for writing any document an agent consumes — a skill, an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, or a doc reached by a pointer. It teaches context pointers (the wording, not the target, decides when material loads; front-load the leading word, one trigger per branch), the two loads every document spends (context load on the agent's window vs cognitive load on the human), the information-hierarchy ladder (in-file steps, in-file reference, disclosed reference behind a pointer) with progressive disclosure and co-location, steps that end on completion criteria (clarity and demand, defending against premature completion), when to split by sequence or invocation, leading words that recruit the model's pretrained concepts, and a pruning discipline (single source of truth, no-ops, sediment). A companion `SKILL-MECHANICS.md` covers frontmatter and invocation mechanics for skills. Discovered via skills.sh. skills.sh Trust Hub check: passed. Honest note: this is a writing reference, not a tool — no scripts, no automation; it changes how you write, not what you run. Fetch `SKILL-MECHANICS.md` with the SKILL.md. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
